headline: High: Dexter’s broad network/API access can leak or act on prompt-injected content, while the prompt-list agent offers no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter has autonomous execution and multiple external inputs, so if it ingests content from awesome-prompts via files or copy-paste, prompt injection is plausible. awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, not a protected executor, so the pair lacks a provenance boundary. The pathway is not documented directly, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Dexter reads prompt text from .dexter/scratchpad/ or pasted content originating from awesome-prompts
IF the prompt repository content is treated as instructions rather than inert reference material
mitigations: Require manual review of imported prompt text before execution
Keep awesome-prompts content in a read-only reference folder
Add a provenance tag to copied prompts before Dexter consumes them
Disable autonomous runs when ingesting untrusted prompt collections
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts shows no touched data classes and no network egress, while Dexter touches financial and market data and can call third-party APIs. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, so leakage between the pair is not evidenced. The main risk is limited to accidental inclusion of sensitive snippets in Dexter’s scratchpad or outputs.
conditions: IF sensitive financial or market data is copied into Dexter’s .dexter/scratchpad/
IF Dexter forwards scratchpad content to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or LangSmith
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of .dexter/scratchpad/
Redact secrets before running Dexter
Review outbound API payloads for copied context
Use separate API keys for non-sensitive test runs
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Because no locking or shared mutable resource is documented, the remaining conflict path is narrow and mostly operational.
conditions: IF multiple Dexter instances write to the same .dexter/scratchpad/ directory
IF another process mutates Dexter scratchpad files during a run
mitigations: Run only one Dexter instance per workspace
Assign separate scratchpad directories per run
Avoid editing scratchpad files mid-run
Check for stale lock or temp files before starting
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared scratchpad writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution can treat upstream text as actionable context, and awesome-prompts is a repository of prompts that may be reused as instructions. If Dexter consumes those prompts without verification, errors or misleading instructions can cascade into generated research outputs and downstream API calls. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dexter uses copied prompts from awesome-prompts as authoritative task instructions
IF Dexter’s outputs are used to trigger API calls or reports without human verification
mitigations: Require a human check before acting on Dexter outputs
Label imported prompts as untrusted templates
Compare Dexter outputs against source documents before use
Limit autonomous runs to non-production tasks
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and sends data to third-party APIs, while awesome-prompts is a prompt repository with no compliance controls shown. The pair therefore creates a compliance gap if regulated financial data is placed into Dexter’s external services. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is entered into Dexter and sent to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or LangSmith
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the copied data
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external APIs
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets for testing
Review vendor terms for each API before production use
Keep prompt repositories free of regulated content
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
